myIndependentMeasurement.instruments: UTF-8 and UTF-16 encoders written by hand inside this review from the encoding definitions, then cross-checked against Python's codecs at 0 disagreements over all 1112064 scalars. No artifact and no corpus checker was read to write them.
myIndependentMeasurement.domain: all valid Unicode scalars 0x0000-0x10FFFF less the surrogate range D800-DFFF
myIndependentMeasurement.whyADJACENTPAIRSSETTLEIT: The scalars form a chain under a total order and encoding-comparison is also a total order, so monotonicity on every adjacent pair extends to every pair by transitivity. Zero adjacent inversions PROVES order-equality; one adjacent inversion DISPROVES it. Both directions are sound.
myIndependentMeasurement.stringLevel: 2379 distinct mixed-plane strings over a pool spanning 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-byte scalars, sorted by scalar order: UTF-8 disagreements 0, UTF-16 disagreements 183. Plus an ALL-PAIRS check over the 182 strings of length <= 2: UTF-8 disagreements 0, UTF-16 disagreements 2508.
myIndependentMeasurement.extentOfTheUTF16Disagreement: Not one pair. Every scalar in [U+E000,U+FFFF] inverts against every scalar >= U+10000 -- 8192 x 1048576 = 8589934592 pairs -- because any supplementary scalar encodes to a lead surrogate in [D800,DBFF] and D800 < E000. Verified on a 200x200 sample at 40000 of 40000 inverting, with the structural reason stated rather than inferred.
myIndependentMeasurement.settlingVector: keys U+E000 and U+10000. U+E000: utf8 ee8080, utf16 units [E000]. U+10000: utf8 f0908080, utf16 units [D800,DC00]. Scalar order emits U+E000 first; UTF-8 order emits U+E000 first; UTF-16 order emits U+10000 first. REPRODUCED EXACTLY as the dispatch describes.
myIndependentMeasurement.myConclusionStatedBeforeReadingTheArtifa: {Unicode scalar value} and {UTF-8 byte order} are THE SAME TOTAL ORDER on characters and on strings. They cannot be distinguished by any bundle, ASCII or otherwise -- not because the corpus is pure ASCII, but because no distinguishing input exists. {UTF-16 code-unit order} is a genuinely different order.

theCentralClaim.verdictOnTheClaim: V1'S CAVEAT WAS FALSE, AND FALSE IN THE WAY v2 SAYS. UTF-8 is order-preserving with respect to code points by construction, so the two 'policies' v1 offered to distinguish are one policy under two names.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- an 'exhaustive' method statement heading a block that contains a sampled, unreproducible measurement
advisories.what: theMeasurement.method reads 'Exhaustive, not sampled. Every valid Unicode scalar 0x0000-0x10FFFF excluding surrogates D800-DFFF.' Three of the block's four measurements are exactly that and I reproduced all three. The fourth, stringLevelCheck, is NOT exhaustive: '18102 distinct strings drawn from a pool spanning 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-byte scalars ... first divergence at index 22.'
advisories.measured: The pool is never stated, so 18102 is not reproducible from the artifact's own text. I searched every product-style pool: no pool size and length bound yields 18102 (pool 26 over lengths 1..3 gives 18278; pool 25 gives 16275). 'First divergence at index 22' is doubly unreproducible, depending on both the unstated pool and its unstated ordering.
advisories.whyItMattersHERESPECIFICALLY: Freeze 7.2.2 requires a recorded measurement to be comparable to the measurement it records. An artifact whose entire subject is a measurement caveat that nobody recomputed should not contain a figure nobody can recompute. It is also the exact criticism B-EIR5-02 levelled at its own subject's evidence -- that reviewer measured 'a stratified sample of 11,465 single code points' and v2 rightly went exhaustive; then labelled a sample 'exhaustive' one line above.
advisories.whyItIsNotABlocker: The string-level CONCLUSION is true and I verified it independently, and it is in any case implied by the exhaustive character-level result: UTF-8 is a prefix-free encoding whose byte sequences preserve code-point order, so order-preservation on characters entails lexicographic order-preservation on strings. The figure is corroboration, not load-bearing.
advisories.repair: Either state the pool and the ordering so the figure is reproducible, or drop the figure and state the entailment -- character-level order-preservation implies string-level -- which is stronger than any sample and costs one sentence. If it is kept, move the 'Exhaustive, not sampled' claim off the block header and onto the three measurements that earn it.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- a correct figure whose key name misstates its referent, understating the result by nine orders of magnitude
advisories.what: utf16VsScalarInversions is reported as 1, under a method statement saying 'Exhaustive ... Every valid Unicode scalar'. Read plainly, that says exactly one pair of scalars disagrees.
advisories.measured: 1 is correct as an ADJACENT-pair count and is not labelled as one. The true number of inverting pairs is 8589934592: every scalar in [U+E000,U+FFFF] inverts against every scalar >= U+10000, because any supplementary scalar opens with a lead surrogate in [D800,DBFF] and D800 < E000. I verified 40000 of 40000 on a sample and state the structural reason rather than inferring it.
advisories.whyItMatters: Freeze 7.2.2's sharpening -- scope by referent, ask what the figure is a measurement OF. A reader deciding how much exposure JCS ordering creates will read '1 inversion' as negligible. It is the opposite: the divergence covers the entire supplementary planes against the upper eighth of the BMP. The artifact's own argument is WEAKER than the truth because of this label.
advisories.repair: Rename to utf16VsScalarAdjacentInversions, or add the total. The adjacent count is the right thing to measure -- it is what settles order-equality -- but its name must say so.

It does NOT repair $.declaredUnresolvedDependencies.entries[4].reproductionStatusInV5, which reads '...cannot distinguish key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-8 bytes.'
advisories.theROOTCAUSEANDWHYITISWORTHSTATING: B-EIR5-02's repair instruction is 'Strike "which differ above the BMP" at both sites', and its paths list names two. That instruction is scoped to the FALSE CLAUSE. The third site carries the VACUITY WITHOUT THE CLAUSE -- it asserts the ASCII bundle cannot distinguish two orderings that are one ordering, and simply stops before the false justification. Both freeze 7.2.2.1 and this subject correctly identify the defect as the vacuity rather than the wrong word; the repair instruction was scoped to the symptom, so it missed the instance that has the disease without the symptom.

advisories.measured: evidence-identity-recipes.v1.review-independent.json ALSO carries the sentence live, at $.whatIDidNotCheck.items[1], and is named by neither. Its wording is uniquely consequential: it does not merely repeat the caveat, it ENDORSES it -- 'The subject's own caveat -- that an all-ASCII bundle cannot distinguish escaping policies for non-ASCII, nor key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-8 bytes -- is correct and I did not narrow it.'
advisories.whyItMatters: Of the permanent record, this is the single entry that affirmatively certifies the false statement as correct, by a reviewer, in a review. Since reviews name reviews individually in both enumerations, its omission is an omission rather than an abbreviation. A reader reconstructing which bytes permanently assert the vacuity will miss the one that validates it.
